No. The plan is yours to keep and works with any developer. If you want us to build it, we can quote the build separately, using the plan as the scope.
What do you need from me?
A short description of the work, access to examples such as emails or tickets, and a call with whoever does the task today. We never need your passwords.
Will you tell me if an agent is a bad idea?
Yes. If a task is better done with a simple automation or by a person, we say so and explain why. Choosing not to build is a perfectly good outcome.
Does the plan include prices for AI usage?
It includes a rough estimate of what the tool and model usage might cost per month, based on your volumes. Real costs depend on the providers you choose and are billed to you directly.

desc:
AI agent planning and task selection helps you choose the right first job for an agent, before you spend on building one. Ecom Swift LLC studies how your team works and writes a plain plan covering the goal, the tools, the limits and how to judge success.

## Why the first task you pick matters

Many agent projects fail for a simple reason: the task was wrong. It was too vague to test, too risky to run alone, or too rare to save any time. Weeks go into building, and the result is an impressive demo that nobody uses.

Planning is the cheap step that prevents this. It asks a few direct questions before any build begins. Is the task frequent? Is it clear enough to describe? What does a mistake cost? Who will check the output? The answers decide whether an agent is a good idea at all.

## What is AI agent planning?

Agent planning is the work of deciding what an agent should do, what it needs and how it will be judged. The output is a written document, not software. It names the task, the goal, the data and tools involved, the permissions it needs, the points where a person approves, and the test that proves it works.

A good plan is useful even if you never hire anyone to build it. You can hand it to your own developer, to another provider or to a no-code builder, and they will know what to make.

## How a good plan affects cost and results

A plan saves money by removing wrong turns. Ranking tasks by time saved and risk shows which job gives the best return, and which should wait. Writing the success measure first means you can tell, after launch, whether the agent is helping or just busy.

It also limits surprises. Listing the risks early lets you design the approvals and limits from the start, rather than adding them after something goes wrong. Teams that plan tend to start smaller, learn faster and expand with confidence.

## What a useful agent plan contains

- A clear description of the task as it is done today, step by step.
- A fit assessment: how often it happens, how clear the rules are and how costly an error would be.
- A goal and a success measure you can check, such as time saved per week or fewer manual corrections.
- The tools, data and access the agent would need, kept as narrow as possible.
- A list of risks and the limits that answer each one.
- Suggested approval points where a person decides.
- Test cases drawn from your real examples.
- A ranking of several candidate tasks with rough effort for each.
- A running-cost estimate, written in general terms, so you know what to budget.
- A recommended build order.

## How we work

We begin with a short conversation about how your team spends its week, and we ask to see real examples: emails, forms, spreadsheets or tickets. We list candidate tasks and score each one for fit and risk. Some tasks will be rejected, and we will say so plainly, since an honest "do not automate this yet" saves you money.

For the tasks that pass, we write the plan. The Basic package assesses one task. Standard compares several tasks, ranks them and adds a working call. Premium goes further and produces a full blueprint for the first agent, with test cases, a permission and approval design and a cost estimate. You can then choose to build with us or with anyone else.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Choose a task that happens often and has a clear right answer.
- Collect real examples, including the awkward ones.
- Decide in advance how you will measure success.
- Name the person who will own the agent after launch.
- Start with a task where a mistake is cheap to fix.

**Avoid:**
- Picking a task because it sounds impressive.
- Giving the agent wide access before you know what it needs.
- Skipping the human review step on the first version.
- Planning ten agents at once.
- Treating the plan as final, when the first results will teach you more.

## Who this is for

This service suits an owner who has heard about agents and wants to know where they would help without taking a risk. It suits a team lead with a long list of ideas who needs them ranked. It also suits a business that tried an agent before, saw it fail and wants to find out why.

## What we need from you

Tell us about your team's recurring work and share a handful of real examples. If we need to look inside your tools, we ask for collaborator, team member or developer access, wherever the platform supports it, with the narrowest permissions. We never ask for passwords.
